title: Triplets With Equal Xor on Both Sides

concept.title: Equal prefix xors, and the number of ways to place the middle
body: Count the triples `(i, j, k)` with `i < j <= k` for which the xor of `a[i..j-1]` equals the xor of `a[j..k]`. If the two xors are equal, the xor of the whole block `a[i..k]` is `0` (because `x ^ x = 0`). With **prefix xors** `P`, the block `a[i..k]` has xor `P[i] ^ P[k+1]`, which is 0 exactly when `P[i] = P[k+1]`.

For such a pair of prefix positions `i < t` (where `t = k + 1`), the middle index `j` can be **any** of `i + 1, ..., t - 1`, which gives `t - i - 1` triples. So every pair of equal prefix xors with indexes `i < t` contributes `t - i - 1`. Summing over all earlier `i` for each `t` is possible without looking at them one by one: keep, for each prefix value, **how many times it occurred** and the **sum of the indexes** where it occurred.
The answer can be as large as `n^3 / 6`, so use 64-bit integers.

statement: Given an array of `n` non-negative integers, count the triples of positions `(i, j, k)` with `i < j <= k` (counting from 1) such that the xor of `a[i], ..., a[j-1]` equals the xor of `a[j], ..., a[k]`.

examples.note: The blocks 2 3 1 and 1 6 7 each have xor 0 and can be split in two ways: the triples (1, 2, 3), (1, 3, 3), (3, 4, 5) and (3, 5, 5).

hints: If both xors are equal, the whole block has xor 0.
Use prefix xors: the block has xor 0 when two prefix xors are equal.
Equal prefixes at positions i < t allow `t - i - 1` choices for the middle position. Keep the count and the index sum of every prefix value.

explanation: Equal prefix xors at positions `i < t` give `t - i - 1` triples. A map of counts and a map of index sums add the contribution of all earlier equal prefixes at once.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

count = {0: 1}
indexSum = {0: 0}
px = 0
total = 0
for t in range(1, n + 1):
    px ^= a[t - 1]
    c = count.get(px, 0)
    total += c * (t - 1) - indexSum.get(px, 0)
    count[px] = c + 1
    indexSum[px] = indexSum.get(px, 0) + t
print(total)
